papers.title_en: Spatial coherence enabled sensorless adaptive optical imaging
papers.authors: Pranay Mohta, Shaurya Aarav, Hugo Defienne, Anand K. Jha
papers.evidence: 为无标记显微镜（包括iSCAT）的像差校正提供无导星自适应光学方法
papers.tldr: 无标记显微成像中缺乏导星，传统无传感器自适应光学校准依赖图像质量指标，其选择受样本与模态影响。本文提出基于空间相干性的无导星AO框架，利用像差导致的测量空间相关分布展宽作为反馈信号。在标准LED照明的明场系统中成功校正相位像差，并在结构背景噪声下依然有效。该工作确立空间相干性测量为有效反馈机制，表明量子辅助AO的相关反馈原理也可用非相干光空间相关实现。
papers.abstract_en: Optical aberrations degrade imaging performance in label-free microscopy, where the absence of a guide star often necessitates sensorless adaptive optics (AO). Conventional sensorless AO approaches rely on image-quality metrics whose optimal choice depends on both the specimen and the imaging modality. Here, we present a guide-star-free AO framework based on the spatial coherence properties of spatially incoherent light. The proposed method exploits aberration-induced broadening of the measured spatial correlation distribution as the feedback signal for aberration correction. Experiments in a conventional bright-field imaging system using standard LED illumination demonstrate successful correction of phase aberrations. Furthermore, the approach remains effective even in the presence of spatially structured background noise. These results establish spatial coherence measurements as an effective feedback mechanism for sensorless AO and indicate that the correlation-based feedback principle employed in quantum-assisted AO can likewise be realized using the spatial correlations of incoherent light.
